description: Three Beacons: briefing, radio calls and outcome text.

briefing: Three practice beacons are set out around the {base}. Fly to within 600 metres of each and hold there for a few seconds. Steer with the mouse or the arrow keys, and use W and S for throttle. Nobody is shooting at you.
success: All three beacons have reported. You can steer, speed up and slow down, which is most of the job.
failure: The beacons are still unlogged. We will set them out again.
radio-near: Pell: The first beacon is close, just off your nose. Steer with the mouse or the arrow keys, and set speed with W and S. Fly in gently and hold beside it.
Pell: Nearest beacon first. W for more speed, S for less, X for none at all. You need to be slow to be counted.
radio-ahead: Pell: Second beacon, a good way ahead. Raise the throttle with W, point at it and go. Ease off with S as you get close, or you will sail past.
Pell: Another one straight ahead, on a long run. Slow down before you arrive, not after.
radio-side: Pell: Last beacon, off to your right. Turn with the mouse, or yaw with A and D. Q and E roll the ship if you want to. Turn until it is ahead of you, then fly in.
Pell: The third is off to the right. Slower speeds turn tighter, so ease off the throttle first.
